content: 1. Pemetrexed and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration may increase the toxicity of either drug due to nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Exercise caution and monitor renal and auditory function closely. 2. Penicillamine and Tenofovir DF: This combination can increase the toxicity of either drug through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Penicillamine may also elevate tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Pentamidine and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs can increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity when used together. Additionally, pentamidine may elevate tenofovir levels. Monitor renal function and drug levels carefully. 4. Tenofovir DF and Peramivir: Tenofovir DF increases peramivir levels by decreasing renal clearance. Caution is advised, especially when peramivir is co-administered with nephrotoxic drugs. Monitor closely. 5. Tenofovir DF and Piroxicam: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance. Modify therapy or monitor closely to avoid potential toxicity. 6. Tenofovir DF and NSAIDs: Co-administration with high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs, which are primarily excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, may increase tenofovir toxicity. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 7. Tenofovir DF and Pramipexole: Tenofovir DF increases pramipexole levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Probenecid and Tenofovir DF: Probenecid increases tenofovir DF levels by decreasing renal clearance, raising the risk of toxicity. Monitor closely and use caution. 9. Tenofovir DF and Procainamide: Tenofovir DF increases procainamide levels by reducing renal clearance, which may lead to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Tenofovir DF and Quinidine: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance. Monitor closely and use caution. 11. Regorafenib and Tenofovir DF: Regorafenib likely inhibits BCRP (ABCG2) transport, increasing systemic exposure to tenofovir DF and related toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 12. Ribavirin and Lamivudine: Ribavirin increases lamivudine toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of lactic acidosis. Modify therapy, monitor closely, and consider alternatives if available. 13. Ritonavir and Doravirine: Ritonavir increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Ritonavir and Lamivudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely and use caution. 15. Ritonavir and Tenofovir DF: Ritonavir increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination, raising the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely and use caution. 16. Rucaparib and Doravirine: Rucaparib increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated and monitor closely. 17. Safinamide and Tenofovir DF: Safinamide and its major metabolite may inhibit intestinal BCRP, increasing tenofovir DF levels. Monitor for pharmacologic or adverse effects of BCRP substrates. 18. Stiripentol and Doravirine: Stiripentol increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for increased plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. 19. Stiripentol and Tenofovir DF: Stiripentol inhibits BCRP transport, potentially increasing tenofovir DF levels. Consider dosage reduction for BCRP substrates if adverse effects occur. 20. Streptomycin and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Streptomycin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Tenofovir DF and Sulindac: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to toxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 22. Tacrolimus and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. 23. Tafamidis and Tenofovir DF: Tafamidis inhibits BCRP in vitro, potentially increasing exposure to tenofovir DF. Dosage adjustment of BCRP substrates may be necessary. 24. Telavancin and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Telavancin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Tipranavir and Lamivudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely and use caution. 26. Tipranavir and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely and use caution. 27. Tenofovir DF and Tobramycin: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Tobramycin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Ublituximab and Doravirine: Ublituximab decreases doravirine effects through immunosuppressive actions, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Tenofovir DF and Tolmetin: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to toxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 30. Tenofovir DF and Trospium Chloride: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Tucatinib and Tenofovir DF: Tucatinib inhibits P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transport, potentially increasing tenofovir DF levels. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates to avoid serious toxicities. 32. Ublituximab and Tenofovir DF: Ublituximab decreases tenofovir DF effects through immunosuppressive actions, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Vadadustat and Tenofovir DF: Vadadustat may increase exposure to tenofovir DF by inhibiting BCRP. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust the dosage of BCRP substrates as needed. 34. Valganciclovir and Lamivudine: Co-administration increases the toxicity of either drug through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of hematologic toxicity. Modify therapy, monitor closely, and consider alternatives if available. 35. Valacyclovir and Tenofovir DF: Valacyclovir increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal function or competing for active tubular secretion. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Tenofovir DF and Vancomycin: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Tenofovir DF and Verapamil: Tenofovir DF increases verapamil levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Voclosporin and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Co-administration may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Voriconazole and Doravirine: Voriconazole increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for increased plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. 40. Lamivudine and Zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely and use caution. 41. Tenofovir DF and Zidovudine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely and use caution. 42. Acyclovir and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Acyclovir also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal function or competing for active tubular secretion. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Adefovir and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Aldesleukin and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Aldesleukin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Amikacin and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Amikacin also increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Tenofovir DF and Amiloride: Tenofovir DF increases amiloride levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Amobarbital and Doravirine: Amobarbital decreases doravirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 48. Amphotericin B (Cholesteryl Sulfate) and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Co-administration may also increase tenofovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Amphotericin B (Deoxycholate) and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Co-administration may also increase tenofovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely.
